title: MZ The use of $gameSystem to save data

posts.author: boomy
posts.body:
Dear plugin creators / javascript aficionados,
Whats the consensus of using $gameSystem to store data for plugins in RPG maker MV/MZ?
I am developing an item upgrade system for MZ and one of the challenges I have to tackle is creating independent items. Game_Item doesn't store any unique data (it only references $dataItems / $dataWeapons etc.) so I have created a map that is saved in $gameSystem that stores a reference to the item as well as assigning the item a unique id. I can now access unique items in the game by calling $gameSystem._uniqueItems (returns a map). As I expand the system to include tracking upgrades for items, all of this data will be saved in $gameSystem.
$gameSystem seems like a noob friendly place to store data; not to mention its globally accessible. I see more advanced plugin makers such as Yanfly make their own class and then hook into the save/load methods to save their data. And then plugins such as SRPG Gear MZ using $gameSystem extensively despite being a fairly complex plugin ecosystem. But is there really any harm in using $gameSystem to store data?

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
A couple of possible issues off the top of my head:
Naming conflicts - another plugin might define a property on
Game_System
with the same name as yours, creating an incompatibility. But this can apply to any approach.
Save residue - in the unlikely event that you use the plugin, make a save, then remove the plugin, any custom data it added to
$gameSystem
would generally remain as bloat.
Like you say, the common alternative is to patch 3
DataManager
methods:
createGameObjects
,
makeSaveContents
, and
extractSaveContents
. That's not really much work either, but it can help to make the resulting plugin more robust.

Excellent answer; I just want to add one thing. If you are really concerned about conflicts, simply add something unique like your name to your attribute. I personally use _mk_ as my initials.
Code:
$gameSystem._mk_independentItems = { }

posts.author: Trihan
posts.body: I do use this method sometimes; if can be a quick-and-dirty way to conveniently add additional data without having to create a completely new game object to do so. I'm wary of it for the same potential risks as caethyril pointed out, though.

Good points.
What if I'm just wanting to create a global variable to track something?
For example, I have a custom font plugin that stores the previous font used.
I'm just using $gameSystem to do this ($gameSystem._fontName)
Would this be a legitimate use?
If I go down the Datamanager methods, I'll also have to use a Imported.Boomy = true (which I seem to see in many plugins), which will temporarily store data (which can then be read or written using dataManager) correct?

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
boomy said:
What if I'm just wanting to create a global variable to track something?
For example, I have a custom font plugin that stores the previous font used.
Click to expand...
If you need it to be saved, then it's the same case as already mentioned.
If it doesn't need to be saved, then storing it on a saved object will bloat saves.
A common approach for (unsaved) global plugin values is to define a global variable of type
object
, i.e. a "namespace". That might be 1 namespace per plugin; it might be a single namespace for the author with properties that are plugin namespaces; it might be some other structure. Data can then be stored as properties of the applicable namespace.
boomy said:
If I go down the Datamanager methods, I'll also have to use a Imported.Boomy = true (which I seem to see in many plugins), which will temporarily store data (which can then be read or written using dataManager) correct?
Click to expand...
No. The
Imported
namespace is just a convention used by many plugin authors to make it easier to check for the existence and/or version of other plugins. It can be useful, e.g. for plugins that extend other plugins. It is not mandatory, and if used conventionally is just constant data.
I guess plugins that create files might save version information etc to those files, but generally
Imported
has nothing to do with the
DataManager
.
